items.followUp: State two characteristics of Kingdom Protista.

rubric.why: Monerans are prokaryotes and lack a membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies Monerans as prokaryotic or lacking a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either key characteristic.

rubric.why: Monerans are generally unicellular and commonly reproduce by binary fission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating they are unicellular or reproduce by binary fission.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Monera consists of unicellular prokaryotic organisms that lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
Many Monerans reproduce asexually by binary fission.

items.followUp: What is meant by scientific naming of organisms?

rubric.why: The term refers to a system in which each organism is given a two-part name.
rubric.description: States that each organism is given a two-part scientific name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the two-part naming system.

rubric.why: The first part is the genus name and the second part is the specific name.
rubric.description: Identifies the two parts as genus and species (specific name).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both parts in the correct order.

modelAnswer: Binomial nomenclature is the system of naming each organism with two words.
The first word is its genus name and the second word is its species (specific) name.

items.followUp: What are leucoplasts, and where are they commonly found?

rubric.why: Chromoplasts are plastids containing coloured pigments other than chlorophyll.
rubric.description: Identifies chromoplasts as coloured, pigment-containing plastids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as pigment-containing plastids.

rubric.why: Their pigments give colour to plant parts such as flowers and fruits.
rubric.description: States that they impart colour to flowers or fruits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct function or example of where their colour is seen.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are plastids that contain coloured pigments other than chlorophyll.
They give colour to parts of plants such as flowers and fruits.

items.followUp: What is the function of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Thylakoid membranes contain photosynthetic pigments that capture light energy.
rubric.description: States that thylakoids capture or absorb light energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the light-absorbing function.

rubric.why: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place in the thylakoids.
rubric.description: Links thylakoids to the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the reaction or process occurring there.

modelAnswer: Thylakoid membranes contain photosynthetic pigments that absorb light energy.
The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place in the thylakoids.

items.followUp: How can a malignant tumour affect tissues beyond its point of origin?

rubric.why: Benign tumours remain localized and do not invade nearby tissues.
rubric.description: Describes a benign tumour as localized or non-invasive.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct distinguishing feature of benign tumours.

rubric.why: Malignant tumours invade nearby tissues and can spread to distant parts of the body.
rubric.description: Describes malignant tumours as invasive or able to spread.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct distinguishing feature of malignant tumours.

modelAnswer: A benign tumour is non-cancerous and remains localized; it does not invade nearby tissues.
A malignant tumour is cancerous, invades surrounding tissues and may spread to other parts of the body.

items.followUp: Define meiosis and state where it occurs.

rubric.why: Mitosis is nuclear division that produces two daughter nuclei, usually yielding two identical cells.
rubric.description: Defines mitosis as nuclear division producing two daughter nuclei or cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the division and its two products.

rubric.why: Mitosis occurs in somatic, or body, cells.
rubric.description: States the cell type in which mitosis occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for somatic or body cells.

modelAnswer: Mitosis is the division of a nucleus to form two genetically identical daughter nuclei.

items.followUp: What is fragmentation? Give an example of an organism that reproduces by it.

rubric.why: Regeneration is the ability to regrow or replace lost body parts.
rubric.description: Defines regeneration as regrowth or replacement of lost body parts.

rubric.why: Planaria and starfish are examples associated with regeneration; a lizard can regrow its tail.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of regeneration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example.

modelAnswer: Regeneration is the ability of an organism to regrow or replace lost body parts.
For example, Planaria can regenerate a complete organism from body pieces.

items.followUp: Name three factors that influence enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Temperature, pH and substrate concentration are factors that affect the rate of enzyme reactions.
rubric.description: Names at least one relevant factor affecting enzyme reaction rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct factor.

rubric.why: Enzyme concentration and the presence of inhibitors or activators can also alter the reaction rate.
rubric.description: Names another relevant factor affecting enzyme reaction rate.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct factor.

modelAnswer: The rate of an enzyme reaction is affected by temperature, pH and substrate concentration.
It is also affected by enzyme concentration and by inhibitors or activators.
